author: Arhaan Raje
title: "Y'all Not Gonna Let This Man Retire": NBA Fans React to LeBron James Reportedly Receiving Invitation to Join USA in 2028 Olympics - NewsBreak
text:
By Arhaan Raje ,
14 hours ago When LeBron James won his third Olympic gold medal with the USA at 39 in 2024, many felt his time with the national team was up. However, it seems that if James wants to have another run at it in 2028, Team USA officials will be open to giving him a roster spot. NBA insider Brian Windhorst reported this on Wednesday.
James will be months away from his 43rd birthday if he decides to play for Team USA in the 2028 Olympics. For now, it seems like a stretch. However, there are compelling reasons why he might consider it. James will have a chance to represent the country at home, in Los Angeles, where he’s lived since 2018.
While he’s moving to the East for the next year and potentially two years, following his move to Philadelphia, his family still resides there. James will also create another unmatched feat as the oldest men’s basketball player to play in the Olympics.
The current record is held by Brazil’s Marcelo Huertas, who was 41 when in the 2024 edition of the tournament. While all this seems intriguing, NBA fans had mixed reactions to the report of Team USA approving James’ wish to play one more tournament.
“Yall not gonna let this man retire,” one fan joked.
More reactions followed.
LeBron James might also retire from the NBA in 2028 LeBron James signed a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers that runs through the 2027-28 season. However, he’s maintained the flexibility for next offseason, as it’s a player option. James can either opt in and continue to play, or opt out, which would allow him to retire or join another franchise in 2027.
If he does play, the 2027-28 season might be his last in the NBA. James would have completed 25 years in the league, allowing him to create another potential unbreakable record.
Rounding off his career with the USA at the LA Olympics would be the dream end to his basketball career. James would still be in shape if he plays the 2027-28 season, so he can be an impactful contributor, even if it’s off the bench.
